items.prompt: For a numeric array x, y=x[1:3] and z=x[1:3].copy(). Which statement matches these operations?

options.text: Changing y can change x; changing z does not change x
options.why: The basic slice shares storage, while this explicit copy owns separate numeric data.

options.text: Both are guaranteed independent deep copies of any Python objects
options.why: A slice is a view, and object-dtype copying has additional reference semantics.

options.text: Changing z always changes x, but y never can
Neither y nor z can ever be modified
options.why: These ordinary arrays are writable unless explicitly restricted.

items.explanation: The stated numeric arrays demonstrate view sharing versus an explicit independent numeric-data copy. Do not extend that claim to nested object references.
